projectName: K8s + OpenTelemetry + Kafka Agent Learning Project
description: Build and deploy a containerized AI agent to AKS with full OpenTelemetry instrumentation, streaming traces through Azure Event Hubs (Kafka) to Databricks Delta Lake
objectives: Understand how agents run in Kubernetes (AKS)
Learn OpenTelemetry Collector architecture and configuration
Build Kafka-based telemetry pipeline with Azure Event Hubs
Ingest traces into Databricks using Auto Loader
Validate end-to-end trace flow from agent to Delta Lake

userStories.title: Extract Agent as Standalone Service
userStories.description: As a developer, I need to extract the todo agent from the existing FastAPI monolith into a standalone microservice so it can be deployed independently
acceptanceCriteria: New directory: agents/k8s-otel-kafka-agent/agent-service/
Agent runs as standalone FastAPI service on port 8080
Single endpoint: POST /process with {message: string}
Returns: {task: string, confidence: float}
OpenTelemetry SDK integrated with OTLP exporter
Environment variables for OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT
Health check endpoint: GET /health
Runs locally with python app.py
technicalNotes: Reuse existing agent logic from ai-todo-app/backend/app/agent.py
Simplify: Remove Databricks writes (just parse task, don't save)
Add OTLP exporter pointing to collector (default: http://localhost:4317)
Use GenAI semantic conventions: gen_ai.request.model, gen_ai.usage.input_tokens
Create span for entire request: agent.process_message
Add nested span for LLM call: openai.chat.completions
Test locally first, OTLP can fail gracefully if collector not running

userStories.title: Containerize Agent with Dockerfile
userStories.description: As a DevOps engineer, I need a Docker image for the agent so it can be deployed to Kubernetes
acceptanceCriteria: Dockerfile in agent-service/ directory
Multi-stage build for small image size
Uses python:3.13-slim base image
Exposes port 8080
Builds successfully: docker build -t agent:local .
Runs locally: docker run -p 8080:8080 -e OPENAI_API_KEY=... agent:local
Health check returns 200 OK
Image size < 500MB
technicalNotes: Use .dockerignore to exclude .env, .venv, __pycache__
COPY requirements.txt first (for caching)
pip install with --no-cache-dir flag
Set PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 for proper logging
Use CMD not ENTRYPOINT for easier overrides
Test with: curl http://localhost:8080/health

userStories.title: Create AKS Cluster and Push Image to ACR
userStories.description: As a DevOps engineer, I need an AKS cluster and the agent image in Azure Container Registry so I can deploy
acceptanceCriteria: AKS cluster created with 1-2 nodes (cheapest SKU)
kubectl configured to connect to AKS
Azure Container Registry (ACR) created
Agent image tagged and pushed to ACR
AKS has pull permissions for ACR
Can run: kubectl get nodes (shows nodes)
Script to automate setup: scripts/setup_aks.sh
technicalNotes: Create resource group: az group create -n rg-k8s-learning -l eastus
Create ACR: az acr create -n <unique-name> -g rg-k8s-learning --sku Basic
Create AKS: az aks create -n aks-learning -g rg-k8s-learning --node-count 1 --node-vm-size Standard_B2s --attach-acr <acr-name>
Get credentials: az aks get-credentials -n aks-learning -g rg-k8s-learning
Build and push: az acr build -r <acr-name> -t agent:v1 ./agent-service
Standard_B2s = cheapest AKS node (~$30/month, can delete after)
Attach ACR to AKS for automatic pull permissions

userStories.title: Deploy OTLP Collector to AKS
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the OpenTelemetry Collector running in Kubernetes so the agent has somewhere to send traces
acceptanceCriteria: OTLP Collector ConfigMap with receivers, processors, exporters
Collector Deployment with 1 replica
Collector Service exposing port 4317 (OTLP gRPC)
Collector configured to export to console (logging exporter) for now
Can view collector logs: kubectl logs -l app=otel-collector
Collector shows 'Everything is ready' in logs
technicalNotes: Use official image: otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:latest
ConfigMap contains collector config YAML
Receivers: otlp (grpc: 4317, http: 4318)
Processors: batch (10s timeout)
Exporters: logging (debug mode), kafka (to be added in US-5)
Service type: ClusterIP (internal only)
Mount ConfigMap as volume: /etc/otel-config.yaml
Container arg: --config=/etc/otel-config.yaml

userStories.title: Deploy Agent to AKS and Verify OTLP Flow
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the agent running in Kubernetes sending traces to the collector
acceptanceCriteria: Agent Deployment with 1 replica
Agent Service exposing port 80 (LoadBalancer or NodePort)
Environment variable OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT set to collector service
Secret for OPENAI_API_KEY
Agent pod is Running (kubectl get pods)
Can call agent: curl http://<external-ip>/process -d '{"message":"buy milk"}'
Collector logs show received spans from agent
End-to-end test: send message → see span in collector logs
technicalNotes: Use image from ACR: <acr-name>.azurecr.io/agent:v1
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT: http://otel-collector:4317
Create secret: kubectl create secret generic openai-key --from-literal=OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
Service type: LoadBalancer (gets public IP) or NodePort for testing
Wait for external IP: kubectl get svc -w
Test from local machine, not inside cluster
Check agent logs: kubectl logs -l app=agent
Check collector logs: kubectl logs -l app=otel-collector

userStories.title: Create Azure Event Hubs and Configure Kafka Exporter
userStories.description: As a data engineer, I need traces flowing from the collector to Azure Event Hubs (Kafka) so Databricks can consume them
acceptanceCriteria: Azure Event Hubs namespace created
Event hub (topic) created: agent-traces
Connection string obtained and stored as K8s secret
OTLP Collector ConfigMap updated with Kafka exporter
Collector redeployed with new config
Traces visible in Event Hubs metrics (incoming messages > 0)
Python consumer script can read traces from Event Hubs
technicalNotes: Create namespace: az eventhubs namespace create -n eh-k8s-learning -g rg-k8s-learning --sku Standard
Create hub: az eventhubs eventhub create -n agent-traces --namespace-name eh-k8s-learning -g rg-k8s-learning
Get connection string: az eventhubs namespace authorization-rule keys list
Event Hubs is Kafka-compatible (port 9093)
Collector Kafka exporter config:
brokers: [<namespace>.servicebus.windows.net:9093]
protocol_version: 2.0.0
topic: agent-traces
auth: SASL PLAIN with connection string
Create K8s secret: kubectl create secret generic eventhub-conn --from-literal=connstring=...
Test with kafka-python consumer script

userStories.title: Databricks Auto Loader - Ingest Traces to Delta Lake
userStories.description: As a data engineer, I need traces from Event Hubs landing in Databricks Delta Lake so I can query them
acceptanceCriteria: Databricks notebook created: ingest_traces_from_kafka.py
Uses Auto Loader (cloudFiles) to read from Event Hubs
Parses OTLP JSON format (nested span structure)
Flattens to table schema: trace_id, span_id, span_name, attributes, timestamp, session_id
Writes to Delta table: main.observability.agent_traces_k8s
Streaming job runs continuously
Can query traces: SELECT * FROM main.observability.agent_traces_k8s
End-to-end test: send agent request → wait 30s → see trace in Delta
technicalNotes: Event Hubs connection string from Azure portal
Use structured streaming with Kafka source
OTLP format: spans are nested JSON (resourceSpans → scopeSpans → spans)
Extract fields: traceId (hex), spanId (hex), name, kind, status
Extract attributes: flatten gen_ai.* fields
Checkpoint location: /mnt/checkpoints/agent_traces_k8s
Schema evolution: mergeSchema option
Latency: ~30-60 seconds from agent to Delta (Event Hubs + streaming micro-batch)
Test query: SELECT span_name, attributes['gen_ai.request.model'] FROM ... WHERE timestamp > current_timestamp() - INTERVAL 5 MINUTES

technicalDecisions.decision: Use AKS instead of Azure Container Apps
technicalDecisions.rationale: Learning goal is Kubernetes. AKS provides full K8s API and transferable skills. Container Apps is simpler but Azure-specific.

technicalDecisions.decision: Use OTLP Collector instead of direct Kafka export from agent
technicalDecisions.rationale: Collector is industry best practice. Decouples agent from backend. Enables buffering, batching, and multi-export without agent code changes.

technicalDecisions.decision: Use Azure Event Hubs instead of Confluent Kafka or Redpanda
technicalDecisions.rationale: Event Hubs is Kafka-compatible, fully managed, and integrates well with Azure ecosystem. Lower operational overhead.

technicalDecisions.decision: Use Databricks Auto Loader instead of Kafka Connect
technicalDecisions.rationale: Auto Loader is native to Databricks, simpler setup, handles schema evolution automatically. No separate Kafka Connect cluster needed.

technicalDecisions.decision: Single replica for agent and collector
technicalDecisions.rationale: Learning project. Single replica is simpler and cheaper. Production would use multiple replicas for HA.
Faster setup. Ingress requires additional controller and TLS config. LoadBalancer gets public IP immediately.

risks.mitigation: Start AKS creation in Hour 2 while working on other tasks. Parallelize work.

risks.risk: OTLP Collector config errors cause silent failures
risks.mitigation: Test collector config locally with docker-compose first. Use logging exporter to validate data flow.

risks.risk: Event Hubs connection string auth issues
risks.mitigation: Test with simple Python consumer before integrating with collector. Validate connection string format.
If time runs out, skip US-8 (documentation). Core pipeline (US-1 to US-7) is the priority.
Use cheapest SKUs (B2s nodes, Basic Event Hubs). Delete resources immediately after learning. Total cost ~$2-5 for 5 hours.

outOfScope: Multiple agent replicas and load testing

timeBreakdown.total: 320 minutes (5h 20m) - target 5 hours by skipping US-8 or working faster
